description: A gate machine built on a binary tree in the shape of the Cantor set: five rows each split in two again and again, with a gate for every cell and a ratio setting how the splits fall

params.text: Sets where this row's cells are split, and with them every row below it; at the centre the split is even
Switches this cell on and off, so a phase passing through it does or does not raise the row's gate output

inputs.text: The phase for this row, a rising 0-10V ramp reading as one pass along the row; with nothing patched the row follows the row above it, and the first row follows the last
Adds to this row's ratio slider, a tenth of its travel per volt

outputs.text: 10V while the phase for this row is inside a cell that is switched on, 0V otherwise
The phase reached inside this row's current cell, 0-10V, while its gate is open, and 0V while it is not

notes: nothing happens until a rising ramp is patched to a phase input; a row with no ramp of its own copies the row above it, and the first row copies the last.
the button at the bottom of the panel switches the display between the ratio sliders and the gate cells; the sliders are hidden while the cells are shown.
click a cell to switch it, drag across cells to set a run of them at once, and double-click a cell to switch every cell in the row below it to that setting.
a polyphonic ramp at a phase input gives a polyphonic gate and phase output with one channel per ramp.
the six gate inputs and the relative-mode switch are declared in the code but have no jack or button on the panel, and relative mode is left switched off.
menu: animate mods — redraws the tree as the ratio modulation moves rather than only when a slider is turned
update cycle — sets how many samples pass between one recalculation and the next, 1 to 1024; a higher number costs less processing and coarsens the gate timing
